groups.label: Competitive Role
groups.description: How a card is used in deckbuilding and play. Requires judgement; supplied by the agent pass, not by the deterministic rules.

groups.label: Effect Function
groups.description: Literal things the card's text (monster text and, for Pendulum monsters, the Pendulum Effect) does. Mostly detected deterministically; the agent may add or correct ambiguous ones.

tags.label: Hand Trap
tags.definition: Has an effect that activates from the hand, usually during the opponent's turn, to disrupt them (often by discarding itself). Examples: Ash Blossom & Joyous Spring, Effect Veiler, Infinite Impermanence, Nibiru the Primal Being, D.D. Crow.

tags.label: Board Breaker
tags.definition: A card used to dismantle or neutralise an established board, usually going second: it removes or negates several cards at once, or wipes the field. Includes symmetric field wipes like Dark Hole, one-sided removal like Raigeki, Lightning Storm, Harpie's Feather Duster and Evenly Matched, blanket negations like Dark Ruler No More and Forbidden Droplet, and tribute-based removal like a Kaiju, Lava Golem or The Winged Dragon of Ra - Sphere Mode. Not every board breaker is one-sided: Dark Hole destroys your own monsters too.

tags.label: Non-Engine
tags.definition: A generic card that is not part of a deck's primary engine or combo: hand traps, board breakers and staples that slot into many decks. Examples: Ash Blossom, Called by the Grave, Crossout Designator, Pot of Prosperity.

tags.label: Starter
tags.definition: Can begin the deck's main combo on its own or almost on its own (one-card or near one-card starter). Examples: Snake-Eye Ash, Aluber the Jester of Despia, Branded Fusion, Tour Guide From the Underworld.

tags.label: Extender
tags.definition: Keeps a combo going, especially after it has been interrupted or a starter has already been used: it provides another body or another play without needing a fresh starter. Example: if Effect Veiler negates Tour Guide From the Underworld while you are going for a Rank 3, Psychic Wheeleder is an extender because it Special Summons itself while you control a Level 3 monster. Examples: Psychic Wheeleder, Psychic Tracker, a free self-summon, a card that revives a combo piece.

tags.label: Engine Requirement
tags.definition: A required named component of a specific archetype's or engine's combo, normally played only inside that engine (a Garnet that must stay in the deck, a mandatory material, an archetype's mandatory piece).

tags.label: Brick
tags.definition: Frequently dead in hand or unable to contribute to the main combo, so drawing it is undesirable. Examples: Red-Eyes Black Dragon in a Dragoon engine, a Garnet that must remain in the deck.

tags.label: Floodgate
tags.definition: A continuous lock that restricts what one or both players can do. Examples: Skill Drain, Dimensional Fissure, Anti-Spell Fragrance, There Can Be Only One, Rivalry of Warlords.

tags.label: Boss Monster
tags.definition: A high-impact monster that acts as a deck's primary win condition or the centrepiece of its end board. Examples: Baronne de Fleur, Mirrorjade the Iceblade Dragon, Borreload Savage Dragon.

tags.label: Disruption
tags.definition: Stops or undoes the opponent's plays during their own turn: hand traps, Traps and Quick Effects that negate or remove.

tags.label: GY Hate
tags.definition: Attacks the opponent's GY: banishing it, shuffling it back, or shutting off effects that use it. Examples: D.D. Crow, Called by the Grave, Soul Drain.

tags.label: Hand Disruption
tags.definition: Discards, removes or reveals cards in the opponent's hand. Examples: Trap Dustshoot, Delinquent Duo, Mind Crush.

tags.label: Protection
tags.definition: Protects its owner's cards from destruction, targeting, negation or effects. Examples: Forbidden Lance, Crossout Designator, Sauravis.

tags.label: Stall
tags.definition: Stops or delays attacks and damage. Examples: Battle Fader, Waboku, Threatening Roar.

tags.label: Alternate Win Condition
tags.definition: Wins or helps win the Duel by an alternate condition. Examples: Exodia the Forbidden One, Final Countdown, Destiny Board, Number iC1000.

tags.label: Control Change
tags.definition: Takes control of an opponent's monster. Examples: Enemy Controller, Mind Control, Change of Heart.

tags.label: Stat Change
tags.definition: Raises or lowers ATK/DEF as a main use. Examples: Limiter Removal, Shrink, Book of Moon is not (position), Megamorph.

tags.label: Battle Trick
tags.definition: Wins or swings a battle when used during the Battle Phase. Examples: Honest, Kalut, Limiter Removal.

tags.label: Searcher
tags.definition: Adds a card from the Deck to the hand. Example: 'add 1 "Snake-Eye" monster from your Deck to your hand'.

tags.label: Special Summons from the Deck
tags.definition: Special Summons a monster from the Deck. Example: 'Special Summon 1 Level 4 monster from your Deck'.

tags.label: Special Summons from the GY
tags.definition: Special Summons a monster from the GY / Graveyard. Example: 'Special Summon 1 "Albaz" monster from your GY'.

tags.label: Special Summons from the Hand
tags.definition: Special Summons a monster from the hand (other than itself). Example: 'Special Summon 1 DARK monster from your hand'.

tags.label: Special Summons from Banishment
tags.definition: Special Summons a monster that is banished / from the banishment. Example: 'Special Summon 1 of your banished monsters'.

tags.label: Special Summons from the Extra Deck
tags.definition: Special Summons a monster directly from the Extra Deck (other than a normal Fusion/Synchro/Xyz/Link Summon). Example: 'Special Summon 1 Fusion Monster from your Extra Deck'.

tags.label: Special Summons Itself
tags.definition: Can Special Summon itself, by effect or its own Summoning procedure. Example: 'Special Summon this card from your hand'.

tags.label: Draws Cards
tags.definition: Draws cards. Example: 'draw 2 cards'.

tags.label: Mills (Deck to GY)
tags.definition: Sends cards from the Deck to the GY, including 'send the top N cards of your Deck to the GY'.

tags.label: Recursion (GY to Hand)
tags.definition: Adds or returns cards from the GY to the hand. Example: 'add 1 monster from your GY to your hand'.

tags.label: Returns to Hand (Bounce)
tags.definition: Returns a card on the field to the hand / owner's hand. Example: 'return that target to the hand'.

tags.label: Returns to Deck (Spin)
tags.definition: Returns or shuffles a card into the Main Deck or Extra Deck. Example: 'shuffle that target into the Deck'.

tags.label: Destroys
tags.definition: Destroys a card or cards by card effect. Example: 'destroy that target'.

tags.label: Banishes
tags.definition: Banishes a card or cards. Example: 'banish that card'.

tags.label: Sends to GY
tags.definition: Sends a card from the hand or field to the GY (not by destroying or discarding it). Example: 'send 1 monster from your hand to the GY'.

tags.label: Discards
tags.definition: Discards a card as a cost or effect. Example: 'discard 1 card'.

tags.label: Tributes
tags.definition: Tributes a monster or monsters. Example: 'Tribute 1 monster'.

tags.label: Negates Activations
tags.definition: Negates the activation of a card or effect. Example: 'negate the activation of that card'.

tags.label: Negates Effects
tags.definition: Negates an effect, or negates the effects of a card on the field. Example: 'negate the effect of that face-up monster'.

tags.label: Negates Summons
tags.definition: Negates a Summon / Special Summon. Example: 'negate the Summon and destroy it'.

tags.label: Negates Attacks
tags.definition: Negates an attack. Example: 'negate the attack'.

tags.label: Generates Tokens
tags.definition: Special Summons a Token. Example: 'Special Summon 1 "Primal Being Token"'.

tags.label: Inflicts Damage
tags.definition: Inflicts effect damage. Example: 'inflict 1000 damage to your opponent'.

tags.label: Gains Life Points
tags.definition: Gains Life Points. Example: 'gain 1000 Life Points'.

tags.label: Pays Life Points
tags.definition: Pays Life Points as a cost. Example: 'pay 1000 Life Points'.

tags.label: Fusion Summons
tags.definition: Performs a Fusion Summon. Example: 'Fusion Summon 1 Fusion Monster'.

tags.label: Synchro Summons
tags.definition: Performs a Synchro Summon. Example: 'Synchro Summon 1 Synchro Monster'.

tags.label: Xyz Summons
tags.definition: Performs an Xyz Summon. Example: 'Xyz Summon 1 Xyz Monster'.

tags.label: Link Summons
tags.definition: Performs a Link Summon. Example: 'Link Summon 1 Link Monster'.

tags.label: Ritual Summons
tags.definition: Performs a Ritual Summon. Example: 'Ritual Summon 1 Ritual Monster'.

tags.label: Pendulum Summons
tags.definition: Performs a Pendulum Summon, or grants an extra Pendulum Summon.

tags.label: Piercing Damage
tags.definition: Deals piercing battle damage. Example: 'piercing battle damage'.

tags.label: Places Counters
tags.definition: Places a counter (Spell Counter, etc.). Example: 'Place 1 Spell Counter on that card'.

tags.label: Removes Counters
tags.definition: Removes a counter as a cost or effect.

tags.label: Attaches Material
tags.definition: Attaches a card to an Xyz Monster as material. Example: 'attach it to that monster as material'.

tags.label: Detaches Material
tags.definition: Detaches Xyz material as a cost or effect.

tags.label: Equips
tags.definition: Equips a card to a monster, or can be equipped. Example: 'equip it to that monster'.

tags.label: Takes Control
tags.definition: Takes control of an opponent's monster. Example: 'take control of that monster'.

tags.label: Excavates
tags.definition: Excavates cards from the top of the Deck. Example: 'excavate the top 3 cards of your Deck'.

tags.label: Reveals or Looks
tags.definition: Reveals or looks at cards in the hand, Deck, Extra Deck or Set cards.

tags.label: Copies Effects
tags.definition: Copies or gains another card's effects / name. Example: 'this card's name becomes "..."', 'gains the effects of...'.

tags.label: Quick Effect
tags.definition: Has a Quick Effect, usable during either player's turn (marked '(Quick Effect)').

tags.label: On-Summon Trigger
tags.definition: Has an effect that triggers when the card is Normal or Special Summoned. Example: 'If this card is Normal or Special Summoned:'.

tags.label: GY Effect
tags.definition: Has an effect that activates or applies while the card is in the GY. Example: 'If this card is in your GY: You can...'.

tags.label: Hand Effect
tags.definition: Has an effect used while the card is in the hand, other than Special Summoning itself (e.g. hand traps, discarding itself for an effect).

tags.label: Banished Effect
tags.definition: Has an effect that activates or applies while the card is banished. Example: 'If this card is banished: You can...'.

tags.label: Battle Protection
tags.definition: Cannot be destroyed by battle, or otherwise protected from battle. Example: 'cannot be destroyed by battle'.

tags.label: Effect Protection
tags.definition: Cannot be destroyed or is unaffected by card effects. Example: 'unaffected by your opponent's card effects'.

tags.label: Targeting Protection
tags.definition: Cannot be targeted by card effects. Example: 'cannot be targeted by card effects'.

tags.label: Restricts Summoning
tags.definition: A player cannot Summon, or can only Summon certain monsters. Example: 'you cannot Special Summon monsters, except DARK monsters'.

tags.label: Restricts Activation
tags.definition: A player cannot activate certain cards or effects, or cannot respond. Example: 'your opponent cannot activate cards or effects in response'.

tags.label: Restricts Attacks
tags.definition: Monsters cannot attack, or attacks are limited. Example: 'monsters your opponent controls cannot attack'.

tags.label: Changes ATK/DEF
tags.definition: Raises, lowers or sets ATK/DEF. Example: 'it gains 500 ATK'.

tags.label: Changes Level/Rank
tags.definition: Changes a Level or Rank. Example: 'its Level becomes 4'.
